Step 4 — Cost Analysis#

Step 3 says what a heat pump can deliver. Step 4, the cost analysis, asks whether it is worth buying. It compares the heat pump with the system it replaces year by year and turns the difference into a net present value, a dynamic payback, the heat cost (LCOH), the CO₂ saving and a break-even electricity price.

The method is the net present value method (Kapitalwertmethode) with price-dynamic cash flows, as in VDI 2067 Blatt 1:2012. Its annuity method, which VDI 4646:2026 builds on, gives the same decision (annuity = NPV × annuity factor). Every input, formula and deviation below names the page of the guideline it comes from. The implementation reproduces the worked examples of both guidelines (see 4.9 Validation).

References. Both are German engineering guidelines of the VDI (Verein Deutscher Ingenieure, Association of German Engineers), published in German and English; the German text is binding.

Short

Guideline

[4646:2026]

VDI 4646:2026-05 Anwendung von Großwärmepumpen (Application of large-scale heat pumps)

[2067-1:2012]

VDI 2067 Blatt 1:2012-09 Wirtschaftlichkeit gebäudetechnischer Anlagen – Grundlagen und Kostenberechnung (Economic efficiency of building installations – Fundamentals and economic calculation)

[GEG 2024]

Gebäudeenergiegesetz 2024, the German Buildings Energy Act, Anlage 9 (CO₂-equivalent factors)

The backend computes every number (/api/analysis/economics). The page, the scenario comparison and the report all show the same results.

4.0 What is compared#

Both systems are costed in full every year:

System

Supplies heat with

Removes the source’s waste heat with

Reference (current situation)

a fuel-fired heater (gas, oil or electric boiler)

today’s cooling, if the source is actively cooled

Heat pump

the heat pump, plus the old heater for whatever the pump does not cover

the heat pump’s evaporator, plus the old cooling for what it does not take

The heat pump is credited only with what it actually replaces. A pump that covers 60 % of the demand leaves 40 % on the old heater, and that remaining fuel stays in its costs.

The pump analysed#

One pump is analysed at a time, so the results stay readable:

  • nothing selected in Step 3 → the default pump the optimization chart highlights (largest duty);

  • one or more selected → the best of the selection: real machines before theoretical archetypes, then the largest heat output, then the highest COP;

  • a click on a point of the Economic heat pump size chart selects that pump.

The reference demand#

The reference must supply the largest demand any candidate could cover, so a small and a large pump are compared against the same current situation:

\[ \texttip{\dot{Q}_{ref}}{Reference heat demand: the largest demand any candidate pump covers [kW]} = \max_p \texttip{\dot{Q}_{demand,total,p}}{Total heat demand seen by pump p [kW]} \qquad \texttip{\dot{Q}_{src,ref}}{Source heat the reference cools today: the largest of the candidates [kW]} = \max_p \texttip{\dot{Q}_{source,p}}{Source heat taken up by pump p [kW]} \]

taken over the analysed pump, the maximum-duty point and all real feasible points of the optimization.

Source code: backend/app/services/economics/model.py (pick_pump, econ_core) 
def pick_pump(
    selected: Sequence[OptimizedIntegrationPoint], opt: Optional[HPIOptimizationResult]
) -> Optional[OptimizedIntegrationPoint]:
    """The one pump analysed, so the analysis stays readable however many are
    picked: the best of the selection (real machines before archetypes, then
    largest heat output, then highest COP). Nothing picked: the default pump, as
    the optimization chart shows."""
    if selected:
        return sorted(selected, key=lambda p: (int(bool(p.theoretical)), -p.Q_demand, -p.COP))[0]
    return opt.max_q_point if opt else None

def econ_core(
    form: Dict[str, float],
    ref_type: str,
    selected: Sequence[OptimizedIntegrationPoint],
    opt: Optional[HPIOptimizationResult],
) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """The numbers alone, no text or charts: what the scenario comparison needs."""
    pump = pick_pump(selected, opt)
    if pump is None:
        return None
    points = [pump]
    inp = to_inputs(form, ref_type)
    # The reference supplies the largest demand (and cools the largest source)
    # among the variants, so every pump is compared against the same Ist-Situation.
    real_feasible = [p for p in (opt.feasible_points if opt else []) if not p.theoretical and p.COP > 0]
    ref_pool = [*points, *([opt.max_q_point] if opt and opt.max_q_point else []), *real_feasible]
    ref_sys = EconReference(
        Q=max(p.Q_demand_total if p.Q_demand_total is not None else p.Q_demand for p in ref_pool),
        Qsrc=max(p.Q_source for p in ref_pool),
    )
    ref = reference_cost(inp, ref_sys)
    # Investment and specific investment are one value seen two ways: I = c_spez · Q.
    # Installed price per kW: the heat pump's own price × planning and
    # installation × integration (VDI 4646 eq. 26 factors).
    spec_total = form["specCost"] * form["fPI"] * form["fPer"]

    def capex_of(p: OptimizedIntegrationPoint) -> int:
        return js_round(spec_total * p.Q_demand)

    variants = [EconVariant(Q=p.Q_demand, Qsrc=p.Q_source, cop=p.COP, capex=capex_of(p)) for p in points]
    results = [evaluate(inp, ref_sys, v) for v in variants]
    break_even = [break_even_el_price(inp, ref_sys, v, inp.pFuel) for v in variants]
    return {
        "pump": pump,
        "points": points,
        "inp": inp,
        "realFeasible": real_feasible,
        "refSys": ref_sys,
        "ref": ref,
        "specTotal": spec_total,
        "capexOf": capex_of,
        "variants": variants,
        "results": results,
        "breakEven": break_even,
    }

Everything else is under More assumptions, in two columns: General, Reference heater, Operating funding, Cooling and Replacement case on the left, Heat pump and Electricity on the right. Every input has a help bulb with typical values.

Options that are off by default have a checkbox. Switching one on fills in the typical value given in the table, and inputs that only count while it is on are greyed out until then.

[!IMPORTANT] Gross and net calorific value. Gas is billed per kWh of gross calorific value \(\texttip{H_s}{Gross calorific value (fuel billed on it)}\), but its CO₂ factor refers to the net calorific value \(\texttip{H_i}{Net calorific value (CO2 factor refers to it)}\) ([4646:2026] p. 60; eq. (23), p. 57 uses \(\texttip{\eta}{Efficiency of the reference heater on Hs, default 87 percent (gas)}_{\texttip{H_s}{Gross calorific value (fuel billed on it)}}\) for the price and \(\texttip{\eta}{Efficiency of the reference heater on Hs, default 87 percent (gas)}_{\texttip{H_i}{Net calorific value (CO2 factor refers to it)}}\) for CO₂). The efficiency, fuel price and fuel consumption are therefore on \(\texttip{H_s}{Gross calorific value (fuel billed on it)}\), and the CO₂ factor is converted with \(\texttip{H_s/H_i}{Ratio of gross to net calorific value, 1,11 for natural gas}\). Using one efficiency for both overstates the CO₂ of gas by about 11 %.

Investment#

The heat pump’s own price per kW times the planning-and-installation and integration factors of [4646:2026] eq. (25)/(26), Tabelle 6, p. 58–59, times the heat output:

\[ \texttip{I}{Investment of the heat pump = price per kW x planning factor x integration factor x heat output [EUR]} = \texttip{c_{spec}}{Heat pump price per kW, machine only, default 1.000 EUR/kW} \cdot \texttip{F_{PI}}{Planning and installation factor, 1,25 (VDI 4646:2026)} \cdot \texttip{F_{Per}}{Integration factor (periphery), default 1,35} \cdot \texttip{\dot{Q}}{Heat output of the heat pump [kW]} \]

Editing the investment sets the price per kW back through the same factors. The default of 1.000 €/kW is the machine alone, from manufacturer offers for large industrial high-temperature heat pumps up to about 150 °C (about 1.000–1.200 €/kW; 175 °C steam about 2.000 €/kW). With the factors, 1.000 × 1,25 × 1,35 ≈ 1.690 €/kW installed, between the Danish Energy Agency values for heat pumps up to 150 °C (1.550 €/kW) and steam heat pumps up to 150 °C (1.750 €/kW).

The full-load hours default to 6.000 h as in [4646:2026]; with a load profile, set \(\texttip{h}{Full-load hours [h/a], default 6.000}\) to the real full-load hours. All inputs are kept for the whole project: every saved scenario is evaluated with the same prices and assumptions, so scenarios differ only in their heat pump.

4.2 Energy flows and CO₂ per year#

The heat pump draws electricity for its duty; the old heater burns fuel for the rest; the old cooling still removes whatever source heat the pump does not take:

\[ \texttip{E_{fuel}}{Fuel used per year, on Hs [kWh/a]} = \frac{(\texttip{\dot{Q}_{ref}}{Reference heat demand: the largest demand any candidate pump covers [kW]} - \texttip{\dot{Q}}{Heat output of the heat pump [kW]}) \cdot \texttip{h}{Full-load hours [h/a], default 6.000}}{\texttip{\eta}{Efficiency of the reference heater on Hs, default 87 percent (gas)}} \qquad \texttip{E_{el}}{Electricity of the heat pump per year [kWh/a]} = \frac{\texttip{\dot{Q}}{Heat output of the heat pump [kW]} \cdot \texttip{h}{Full-load hours [h/a], default 6.000}}{\texttip{COP}{Coefficient of performance of the heat pump}} \qquad \texttip{E_{cool}}{Electricity of the remaining cooling per year [kWh/a]} = \frac{(\texttip{\dot{Q}_{src,ref}}{Source heat the reference cools today: the largest of the candidates [kW]} - \texttip{\dot{Q}_{src}}{Source heat the heat pump takes up (its evaporator) [kW]}) \cdot \texttip{h}{Full-load hours [h/a], default 6.000} \cdot a}{\texttip{EER}{Cooling COP of today's cooling, default 4}} \]

For the reference, \(\texttip{\dot{Q}}{Heat output of the heat pump [kW]} = \texttip{\dot{Q}_{src}}{Source heat the heat pump takes up (its evaporator) [kW]} = 0\) and \(\texttip{E_{el}}{Electricity of the heat pump per year [kWh/a]} = 0\).

CO₂ emissions follow from the same flows, with \(\texttip{E_{fuel}}{Fuel used per year, on Hs [kWh/a]}\) on \(\texttip{H_s}{Gross calorific value (fuel billed on it)}\) ([4646:2026] eq. (30)/(31), p. 63):

\[ \texttip{CO_2}{CO2 emissions per year [t/a]} = \frac{\texttip{E_{fuel}}{Fuel used per year, on Hs [kWh/a]}}{\texttip{H_s/H_i}{Ratio of gross to net calorific value, 1,11 for natural gas}} \cdot \texttip{c_{CO_2}}{CO2 factor of the fuel on Hi (gas 0,201 t/MWh)} + (\texttip{E_{el}}{Electricity of the heat pump per year [kWh/a]} + \texttip{E_{cool}}{Electricity of the remaining cooling per year [kWh/a]}) \cdot \texttip{c_{CO_2,el}}{CO2 factor of electricity, 0,352 t/MWh} \]

With CO₂ balance in CO₂-equivalents on (the default), the same formula uses \(\texttip{c_{CO_2e}}{CO2-equivalent factor of the fuel incl. upstream chain, on Hi (gas 0,24 t/MWh)}\) and \(\texttip{c_{CO_2e,el}}{CO2-equivalent factor of electricity incl. upstream chain, 0,56 t/MWh (GEG 2024)}\): CO₂-equivalents including the upstream chain (methane, nitrous oxide, extraction and transport), [GEG 2024] Anlage 9. The CO₂ rows are then labelled “(CO₂e)”. The CO₂ costs in 4.3 always use the pure CO₂ factors \(\texttip{c_{CO_2}}{CO2 factor of the fuel on Hi (gas 0,201 t/MWh)}\), \(\texttip{c_{CO_2,el}}{CO2 factor of electricity, 0,352 t/MWh}\): BEHG and EU ETS price only the CO₂ from combustion.

Final energy saving is the difference in final energy, fuel and electricity alike:

\[ \texttip{\Delta E}{Final energy saving per year [kWh/a]} = (\texttip{E_{fuel}}{Fuel used per year, on Hs [kWh/a]} + \texttip{E_{cool}}{Electricity of the remaining cooling per year [kWh/a]})_{ref} - (\texttip{E_{fuel}}{Fuel used per year, on Hs [kWh/a]} + \texttip{E_{el}}{Electricity of the heat pump per year [kWh/a]} + \texttip{E_{cool}}{Electricity of the remaining cooling per year [kWh/a]})_{HP} \]

4.3 Prices over time#

Prices are given for year 0 and change from year 1 at their own rates. The fuel carries a CO₂ cost with its own price path:

\[ \texttip{p_{fuel}}{Fuel price in year t incl. CO2 cost [EUR/kWh]}(t) = \texttip{p_{fuel,0}}{Fuel price today, excl. CO2, per kWh Hs [ct/kWh], default 6} \cdot (1 + \texttip{r_{fuel}}{Yearly fuel price change, default 3 percent})^t + \frac{\texttip{c_{CO_2}}{CO2 factor of the fuel on Hi (gas 0,201 t/MWh)}}{1000 \cdot \texttip{H_s/H_i}{Ratio of gross to net calorific value, 1,11 for natural gas}} \cdot \texttip{p_{CO_2,0}}{CO2 price today, default 55 EUR/t} \cdot (1 + \texttip{r_{CO_2}}{Yearly CO2 price change, default 0})^t \]
\[ \texttip{p_{el}}{Electricity price in year t [EUR/kWh]}(t) = \texttip{p_{el,0}}{Electricity price today [ct/kWh], default 13} \cdot (1 + \texttip{r_{el}}{Yearly electricity price change, default 3 percent})^t \;\big[ + \tfrac{\texttip{c_{CO_2,el}}{CO2 factor of electricity, 0,352 t/MWh}}{1000} \cdot \texttip{p_{CO_2,0}}{CO2 price today, default 55 EUR/t} \cdot (1 + \texttip{r_{CO_2}}{Yearly CO2 price change, default 0})^t \big] \]

The bracket counts only when Add CO₂ cost on electricity is on. This is [4646:2026] eq. (23) and (29), p. 57 and 61. [4646:2026] assumes constant prices (all \(r = 0\), p. 57). The app’s default is +3 %/a for fuel and electricity (CO₂ and investment 0 %): a deliberate deviation, allowed by [2067-1:2012] §6.9, p. 12, which permits change rates per cost type. The same rate on both sides keeps the electricity-to-gas price ratio constant; set both to 0 for the VDI 4646:2026 case. Today’s price grown by one year equals the “first-year cost” \(A_{V1}\) of [2067-1:2012] eq. (6), so the two conventions agree.

Source code: backend/app/services/economics/formulas.py (fuel_price, el_price) 
def fuel_price(inp: EconInputs, t: float) -> float:
    """Fuel price incl. CO₂ cost in year t, € per kWh_Hs. The CO₂ factor is per
    kWh_Hi, so per kWh_Hs it is divided by Hs/Hi."""
    co2 = (inp.co2Fuel / inp.hsHi / 1000) * _co2_at(inp, t) if inp.co2Priced else 0
    return inp.pFuel * (1 + inp.rFuel) ** t + co2

def el_price(inp: EconInputs, t: float) -> float:
    """Electricity price in year t, €/kWh, with its CO₂ cost when that is not
    already in the price."""
    return inp.pEl * (1 + inp.rEl) ** t + ((inp.co2El / 1000) * _co2_at(inp, t) if inp.co2ElPriced else 0)

4.4 Operating costs per year#

\[ \texttip{K}{Operating costs in year t [EUR]}(t) = \texttip{E_{fuel}}{Fuel used per year, on Hs [kWh/a]} \cdot \texttip{p_{fuel}}{Fuel price in year t incl. CO2 cost [EUR/kWh]}(t) + (\texttip{E_{el}}{Electricity of the heat pump per year [kWh/a]} + \texttip{E_{cool}}{Electricity of the remaining cooling per year [kWh/a]}) \cdot \texttip{p_{el}}{Electricity price in year t [EUR/kWh]}(t) + \texttip{f_M}{Maintenance per year as share of the investment, 2,5 percent} \cdot \texttip{I}{Investment of the heat pump = price per kW x planning factor x integration factor x heat output [EUR]} + \texttip{t_{AB}}{Operation effort [h/a], default 5} \cdot \texttip{w}{Hourly rate for operation, default 100 EUR/h} + \texttip{p_C}{Capacity charge [EUR per kW el and year], default off} \cdot \texttip{P_{el}}{Electrical power of the heat pump = heat output / COP [kW]} - \texttip{f_{k,ref}}{Maintenance of the avoided boiler, 3 percent per year} \cdot \texttip{I_{ref}}{Avoided boiler investment = boiler price per kW x heat output (0 in the efficiency case)} - \texttip{F_{op}}{Operating funding received in year t [EUR]}(t) \]

with \(\texttip{P_{el}}{Electrical power of the heat pump = heat output / COP [kW]} = \texttip{\dot{Q}}{Heat output of the heat pump [kW]} / \texttip{COP}{Coefficient of performance of the heat pump}\), the avoided boiler investment \(\texttip{I_{ref}}{Avoided boiler investment = boiler price per kW x heat output (0 in the efficiency case)} = \texttip{c_{boiler}}{Avoided boiler investment per kW of heat pump (replacement case), 200 EUR/kW when on} \cdot \texttip{\dot{Q}}{Heat output of the heat pump [kW]}\) (0 in the default efficiency case) and the operating funding

\[\begin{split} \texttip{F_{op}}{Operating funding received in year t [EUR]}(t) = \begin{cases} \texttip{f_{op}}{Operating funding per MWh of heat, default off} \cdot \texttip{\dot{Q}}{Heat output of the heat pump [kW]} \cdot \texttip{h}{Full-load hours [h/a], default 6.000} & t \le \texttip{t_{op}}{Years the operating funding is paid, default 10} \\ 0 & \text{otherwise} \end{cases} \end{split}\]

These are the demand-related, operation-related and maintenance costs of [2067-1:2012] eq. (6)–(9), p. 18–19, and [4646:2026] eq. (22)–(28), p. 57–60. Maintenance, operation, capacity charge, the saved boiler maintenance and operating funding apply to the heat pump only. The cost saving in year 1 is \(\texttip{S}{Cost saving in year 1 [EUR]}(1) = \texttip{K_{ref}}{Operating costs of the reference in year t [EUR]}(1) - \texttip{K_{HP}}{Operating costs with the heat pump in year t [EUR]}(1)\) (in the result table).

Source code: backend/app/services/economics/formulas.py (_flows) 
def _flows(inp: EconInputs, ref: EconReference, v: Optional[EconVariant]) -> _Flows:
    """Energy flows and fixed costs of a system: the reference alone (v = None)
    or a heat pump with the reference covering what the pump leaves."""
    fuel = (max(ref.Q - (v.Q if v else 0), 0) * inp.hours) / inp.eta
    el = (v.Q * inp.hours) / v.cop if v and v.cop > 0 else 0
    el_cool = (
        (max(ref.Qsrc - (v.Qsrc if v else 0), 0) * inp.hours * inp.coolShare) / inp.eer
        if inp.eer > 0
        else 0
    )
    p_el_kw = v.Q / v.cop if v and v.cop > 0 else 0
    # Heat pump only: maintenance, operation, capacity charge; minus the
    # maintenance of a boiler that no longer has to be bought (replacement case).
    fixed = (
        inp.fMaint * v.capex + inp.opHours * inp.wage + inp.pDemand * p_el_kw
        - inp.fMaintRef * inp.boilerInvest * v.Q
        if v
        else 0
    )

    def cost(t: int) -> float:
        # Operating funding lowers the heat pump's cost while it is paid.
        return (
            fuel * fuel_price(inp, t)
            + (el + el_cool) * el_price(inp, t)
            + fixed
            - (inp.opFunding * v.Q * inp.hours if v and t <= inp.opFundingYears else 0)
        )

    return _Flows(
        fuel=fuel,
        el=el,
        elCool=el_cool,
        co2=(
            (fuel / inp.hsHi) * (inp.co2Fuel if inp.co2eFuel is None else inp.co2eFuel)
            + (el + el_cool) * (inp.co2El if inp.co2eEl is None else inp.co2eEl)
        ) / 1000,
        cost=cost,
    )

4.5 Net present value#

The yearly cash flow is what the heat pump saves against the reference:

\[ \texttip{CF}{Cash flow in year t: what the heat pump saves [EUR]}(t) = \texttip{K_{ref}}{Operating costs of the reference in year t [EUR]}(t) - \texttip{K_{HP}}{Operating costs with the heat pump in year t [EUR]}(t) \]

The net present value discounts every cash flow to year 0, after the investment net of funding, the avoided boiler investment, any reinvestment \(\texttip{R}{Replacements and reinvestment in year t [EUR]}(t)\) and the residual value at the end of the period:

\[ \texttip{NPV}{Net present value (Kapitalwert) [EUR]} = -(1 - \texttip{\varphi}{Investment funding as share of the investment, default 0}) \cdot \texttip{I}{Investment of the heat pump = price per kW x planning factor x integration factor x heat output [EUR]} + \texttip{I_{ref}}{Avoided boiler investment = boiler price per kW x heat output (0 in the efficiency case)} + \sum_{t=1}^{\texttip{T}{Period of analysis [a], default 20}} \frac{\texttip{CF}{Cash flow in year t: what the heat pump saves [EUR]}(t) - \texttip{R}{Replacements and reinvestment in year t [EUR]}(t)}{(1 + \texttip{i}{Discount rate, default 8 percent})^t} + \frac{\texttip{RV}{Residual value after T years [EUR]}}{(1 + \texttip{i}{Discount rate, default 8 percent})^\texttip{T}{Period of analysis [a], default 20}} \]

\(\texttip{R}{Replacements and reinvestment in year t [EUR]}(t)\) are the replacements of [2067-1:2012] eq. (1)–(2), p. 16–17 — the heat pump is bought again at the end of each service life, at the then-current price — plus the optional reinvestment (share × \(\texttip{I}{Investment of the heat pump = price per kW x planning factor x integration factor x heat output [EUR]}\) in its year):

\[ \texttip{R}{Replacements and reinvestment in year t [EUR]}(t) = \texttip{I}{Investment of the heat pump = price per kW x planning factor x integration factor x heat output [EUR]} \cdot (1 + \texttip{r_{inv}}{Yearly price change of the investment, default 0})^t \quad \text{at } t = \texttip{L}{Service life of the heat pump, 20 a}, 2\texttip{L}{Service life of the heat pump, 20 a}, \dots < \texttip{T}{Period of analysis [a], default 20} \]

The residual value is the last purchase, depreciated linearly over its service life ([2067-1:2012] eq. (3), p. 17):

\[ \texttip{RV}{Residual value after T years [EUR]} = \texttip{I}{Investment of the heat pump = price per kW x planning factor x integration factor x heat output [EUR]} \cdot (1 + \texttip{r_{inv}}{Yearly price change of the investment, default 0})^{nL} \cdot \frac{(n+1) \cdot \texttip{L}{Service life of the heat pump, 20 a} - \texttip{T}{Period of analysis [a], default 20}}{\texttip{L}{Service life of the heat pump, 20 a}}, \qquad n = \lceil \texttip{T}{Period of analysis [a], default 20}/\texttip{L}{Service life of the heat pump, 20 a} \rceil - 1 \]

A positive NPV means the heat pump earns more over \(\texttip{T}{Period of analysis [a], default 20}\) years than the money would earn at the discount rate \(\texttip{i}{Discount rate, default 8 percent}\). The annuity of [2067-1:2012] eq. (12) / [4646:2026] eq. (22) is the same result spread over the years: \(A = \texttip{NPV}{Net present value (Kapitalwert) [EUR]} \cdot a\) with the annuity factor \(a = \texttip{i}{Discount rate, default 8 percent} / (1 - (1+\texttip{i}{Discount rate, default 8 percent})^{-\texttip{T}{Period of analysis [a], default 20}})\) ([2067-1:2012] eq. (4), p. 17; [4646:2026] eq. (24), p. 57).

4.6 Dynamic payback#

The dynamic payback is the time until the cumulated, discounted cash flows have recovered the net investment:

\[ \texttip{NPV}{Net present value (Kapitalwert) [EUR]}(k) = -(1 - \texttip{\varphi}{Investment funding as share of the investment, default 0}) \cdot \texttip{I}{Investment of the heat pump = price per kW x planning factor x integration factor x heat output [EUR]} + \texttip{I_{ref}}{Avoided boiler investment = boiler price per kW x heat output (0 in the efficiency case)} + \sum_{t=1}^{k} \frac{\texttip{CF}{Cash flow in year t: what the heat pump saves [EUR]}(t) - \texttip{R}{Replacements and reinvestment in year t [EUR]}(t)}{(1 + \texttip{i}{Discount rate, default 8 percent})^t}, \qquad k^* = \min \{ k : \texttip{NPV}{Net present value (Kapitalwert) [EUR]}(k) \ge 0 \} \]

Within the year \(k^*\) it is interpolated linearly, so it has one decimal:

\[ \texttip{t_P}{Dynamic payback [a], one decimal} = k^* - 1 + \frac{-\texttip{NPV}{Net present value (Kapitalwert) [EUR]}(k^*-1)}{\texttip{NPV}{Net present value (Kapitalwert) [EUR]}(k^*) - \texttip{NPV}{Net present value (Kapitalwert) [EUR]}(k^*-1)} \]

It is shown as “8,2 years / 2035”: the years, and the calendar year \(\texttip{t_0}{First year of operation = year 0 (investment paid)} + \lceil \texttip{t_P}{Dynamic payback [a], one decimal} \rceil\) in which it is reached. The search runs past \(\texttip{T}{Period of analysis [a], default 20}\) up to 40 years, so a pump that pays back after the period still gets a value. The residual value is left out here: it is not cash in hand before the end of the period.

Source code: backend/app/services/economics/formulas.py (evaluate) 
def evaluate(inp: EconInputs, ref: EconReference, v: EconVariant, with_irr: bool = True) -> dict:
    """All results of one heat pump. `with_irr=False` skips the internal rate
    of return, the one costly result, where only the NPV is wanted."""
    r = _flows(inp, ref, None)
    h = _flows(inp, ref, v)
    # A boiler that no longer has to be bought counts as income at t = 0.
    net_invest = (1 - inp.funding) * v.capex - inp.boilerInvest * v.Q

    def rate(t: float) -> float:
        return (1 + inp.i) ** t

    npv_curve: List[float] = [-net_invest]
    npv = -net_invest
    # Years to pay back, interpolated within the year the Kapitalwert turns positive.
    payback: Optional[float] = 0 if npv >= 0 else None
    cum_cost = 0.0
    for t in range(1, int(max(inp.T, PAYBACK_HORIZON)) + 1):
        cost = h.cost(t)
        reinvest = (inp.reinvestShare * v.capex if t == inp.reinvestYear else 0) + _replacement(inp, v.capex, t)
        prev = npv
        npv += (r.cost(t) - cost - reinvest) / rate(t)
        if payback is None and npv >= 0:
            payback = t - 1 + -prev / (npv - prev)
        if t <= inp.T:
            npv_curve.append(npv)
            cum_cost += cost

    # Counted in the Kapitalwert, not in the payback curve.
    residual = residual_value(inp, v.capex)
    npv_T = npv_curve[-1] + residual / rate(inp.T)
    saving1 = r.cost(1) - h.cost(1)

    # LCOH (VDI 4646 eq. 21–23): annuity of a heater's costs over the heat it
    # makes. The heat pump: capital (net of funding, with replacements, less
    # residual value) + maintenance and operation + its electricity, of which
    # only the share α is charged to heating. The reference heater: its fuel.
    a = annuity_factor(inp.i, inp.T)
    heat = v.Q * inp.hours
    alpha = allocation_factor(inp, v.cop)
    pv_hp = (1 - inp.funding) * v.capex - residual / rate(inp.T)
    pv_ref = inp.boilerInvest * v.Q
    p_el_kw = v.Q / v.cop if v.cop > 0 else 0
    for t in range(1, int(inp.T) + 1):
        own = (
            alpha * h.el * el_price(inp, t)
            + inp.fMaint * v.capex
            + inp.opHours * inp.wage
            + inp.pDemand * p_el_kw
            - (inp.opFunding * heat if t <= inp.opFundingYears else 0)
        )
        pv_hp += (own + _replacement(inp, v.capex, t)) / rate(t)
        pv_ref += ((heat / inp.eta) * fuel_price(inp, t) + inp.fMaintRef * inp.boilerInvest * v.Q) / rate(t)

    return {
        "fuel": h.fuel,
        "el": h.el,
        "elCool": h.elCool,
        "co2": h.co2,
        "opex1": h.cost(1),
        "energySaving": r.fuel + r.elCool - (h.fuel + h.el + h.elCool),
        "saving1": saving1,
        "co2Saving": r.co2 - h.co2,
        "npvCurve": npv_curve,
        "residual": residual,
        "npv": npv_T,
        "payback": payback,
        "paybackStatic": 0 if net_invest <= 0 else (net_invest / saving1 if saving1 > 0 else None),
        "irr": _internal_rate(inp, ref, v) if with_irr else None,
        "lcohHp": (a * pv_hp) / heat if heat > 0 else 0,
        "lcohRef": (a * pv_ref) / heat if heat > 0 else 0,
        "alpha": alpha,
        "cumCost": cum_cost,
    }

4.7 Break-even electricity price#

For a given fuel price, the break-even electricity price \(\texttip{p_{el}^*}{Break-even electricity price: NPV = 0, below it the heat pump wins}\) is the one at which the NPV is exactly zero. Below it the heat pump wins. The NPV is linear in the electricity price, so two evaluations give the root exactly:

\[ \texttip{p_{el}^*}{Break-even electricity price: NPV = 0, below it the heat pump wins} = -\frac{\texttip{NPV}{Net present value (Kapitalwert) [EUR]}(\texttip{p_{el}}{Electricity price in year t [EUR/kWh]} = 0)}{\texttip{NPV}{Net present value (Kapitalwert) [EUR]}(\texttip{p_{el}}{Electricity price in year t [EUR/kWh]} = 1) - \texttip{NPV}{Net present value (Kapitalwert) [EUR]}(\texttip{p_{el}}{Electricity price in year t [EUR/kWh]} = 0)} \]
Source code: backend/app/services/economics/formulas.py (break_even_el_price) 
def break_even_el_price(inp: EconInputs, ref: EconReference, v: EconVariant, p_fuel: float) -> Optional[float]:
    """Electricity price [€/kWh] at which the Kapitalwert is exactly 0 for a given
    fuel price: below it the heat pump beats the reference. The Kapitalwert is
    linear in the electricity price, so two evaluations pin the root exactly.
    None when the electricity price has no effect."""
    def at(p_el: float) -> float:
        return npv_at(dc_replace(inp, pFuel=p_fuel, pEl=p_el), ref, v, inp.i)

    npv0 = at(0)
    slope = at(1) - npv0
    return -npv0 / slope if slope < 0 else None

the discount rate at which \(\texttip{NPV}{Net present value (Kapitalwert) [EUR]} = 0\)

[4646:2026] eq. (C6), p. 91

\(k_{Inv} = F_{WP} \, \texttip{\dot{Q}}{Heat output of the heat pump [kW]}^{E_{WP}} \cdot 1{,}25 \cdot 1{,}8 / \texttip{\dot{Q}}{Heat output of the heat pump [kW]}\)

[4646:2026] eq. (26), Tabelle 6, p. 58–59

\(\texttip{R_L}{Replacement purchases at the end of each service life [EUR]}(t)\) are the replacements at the end of each service life (the optional reinvestment is not in the LCOH). Both heat costs are for the heat the pump makes, \(\texttip{\dot{Q}}{Heat output of the heat pump [kW]} \texttip{h}{Full-load hours [h/a], default 6.000}\), so they compare like with like.

Finnish method. When the heat pump’s cold side replaces cooling, the pump makes two products, heat and cold. Its electricity is split by what each would cost made separately: heat from the boiler (\(\texttip{COP}{Coefficient of performance of the heat pump}/\texttip{\eta}{Efficiency of the reference heater on Hs, default 87 percent (gas)}\)), cold from the existing cooling (\(a \cdot (\texttip{COP}{Coefficient of performance of the heat pump}-1)/\texttip{EER}{Cooling COP of today's cooling, default 4}\)). Only the share \(\texttip{\alpha}{Allocation factor (Finnish method): share of the electricity charged to heat}\) is charged to heat. The app multiplies the cooling term by the actively cooled share \(a\) — an extension of [4646:2026], whose formula assumes the whole cold side is useful (the case \(a = 1\)); cold that replaces no chiller earns no credit, so with \(a = 0\), \(\texttip{\alpha}{Allocation factor (Finnish method): share of the electricity charged to heat} = 1\). The NPV and payback need no split: they compare the whole systems, heating and cooling, as in [4646:2026] Bild 9, p. 54.

Source code: backend/app/services/economics/formulas.py (allocation_factor, vdi_specific_cost) 
def allocation_factor(inp: EconInputs, cop: float) -> float:
    """Finnish allocation factor (VDI 4646 eq. 17/18): the share of the heat
    pump's electricity that is charged to heating when its cold side also
    replaces cooling. Only the actively cooled share of the source heat counts
    as useful cooling, so with nothing cooled today α = 1."""
    heat = cop / inp.eta
    cold = (inp.coolShare * max(cop - 1, 0)) / inp.eer if inp.eer > 0 else 0
    return heat / (heat + cold)

def vdi_specific_cost(Q: float) -> float:
    """VDI 4646 cost function (eq. 25/26, Tabelle 6): specific investment of a
    large heat pump incl. planning, installation and integration, €/kW_th.
    Shown for reference only; the app's default comes from newer literature."""
    if Q <= 0:
        return 0
    F, E = (1521, 0.637) if Q <= 210 else (349.5, 0.912)
    return (F * Q ** E * 1.25 * 1.8) / Q

What the page shows#

Key results (one card each): dynamic payback (\(\texttip{t_P}{Dynamic payback [a], one decimal}\), 4.6), net present value (4.5), heat cost of the heat pump with the reference’s underneath (4.8), CO₂ saving (4.2) and break-even electricity price (4.7). Every result row has a help bulb with its formula and source.

Chart

What it shows

Costs over \(\texttip{T}{Period of analysis [a], default 20}\) years

One stacked bar per system: the nominal (undiscounted) operating costs over \(\texttip{T}{Period of analysis [a], default 20}\), with the investment on top. In the replacement case the reference bar carries the boiler investment it would have to make (\(\texttip{c_{boiler}}{Avoided boiler investment per kW of heat pump (replacement case), 200 EUR/kW when on} \cdot \texttip{\dot{Q}}{Heat output of the heat pump [kW]}\)). The total is written above each bar; the legend gives the investment’s share.

Energy price development

\(\texttip{p_{fuel}}{Fuel price in year t incl. CO2 cost [EUR/kWh]}(t)\) with and without CO₂, and \(\texttip{p_{el}}{Electricity price in year t [EUR/kWh]}(t)\) over the period.

NPV over time

\(\texttip{NPV}{Net present value (Kapitalwert) [EUR]}(k)\) year by year, past \(\texttip{T}{Period of analysis [a], default 20}\) until payback; red markers before payback, green after; a dotted line marks the end of the period. The legend names the payback year.

Sensitivity map

NPV for every pair of fuel and electricity prices, each from 0 to twice the entered price (at most about 14 cells per axis). Cells are red where the reference is cheaper and green where the heat pump pays off; the dashed line between them is \(\texttip{p_{el}^*}{Break-even electricity price: NPV = 0, below it the heat pump wins}\), with the exact price pair on hover. The “WP” box marks the entered prices. Clicking a cell or the line adopts its prices everywhere.

Economic heat pump size

NPV against heat output for every real pump on the profiles, keeping the best machine per 1 % of the demand. A smaller pump costs less but leaves more on the old heater; the peak is the economic optimum (open gold ring). The analysed pump is the “WP” box; when it is the optimum, the ring sits around the box. Clicking a point analyses that pump. Source- and demand-limited pumps are left out, as on the optimization chart: on-profile pumps come in duty steps wider than 1 %, so a source-limited pump (partial coverage at a high sink temperature, poor COP) landing in an empty step would otherwise pull the curve down to a loss.

A plain-language summary closes the section: coverage, energy and CO₂ saved, cost saving, investment, payback, NPV and break-even price of the pump analysed.

Scenario comparison and report#

  • Scenario comparison: each saved scenario gets its investment, NPV, dynamic payback and cost saving in year 1, plus a bar chart of NPV per scenario. All scenarios use the same inputs.

  • Report: every scenario page ends with the full cost analysis — key results, all inputs, both result tables, the charts and the summary. The comparison page carries the same economic columns and the NPV-per-scenario chart.

export function econReportData(t: TFunction, form: Form, refType: RefType, n: EconNumbers | null) {
  const e = buildEconomics(t, form, refType, n);
  if (!e) return null;
  const fmtInput = (key: keyof Form) =>
    BOOL_FIELDS.includes(key)
      ? t(form[key] ? 'economics.yes' : 'economics.no')
      : formatDe(form[key], 4, key !== 'year' && key !== 'reinvestYear');
  return {
    title: t('economics.title'),
    pump: pointName(e.pump),
    labels: {
      key: t('economics.blocks.results'),
      inputs: t('economics.report_inputs'),
      results: t('economics.report_results'),
      charts: t('economics.blocks.charts'),
      sensitivity: t('economics.blocks.sensitivity'),
      size: t('economics.blocks.size'),
      summary: t('economics.blocks.summary'),
    },
    kpis: e.kpis,
    inputs: GROUPS.map((g) => ({
      title: t(`economics.groups.${g}`),
      rows: [
        ...(g === 'reference'
          ? [[t('economics.inputs.refType'), t(`economics.ref.${refType}`), '']]
          : []),
        ...FIELDS.filter((f) => f[2] === g).map(([key, unit]) => [
          t(`economics.inputs.${key}`, { fuel: e.fuel }),
          fmtInput(key),
          e.unitLabel(unit),
        ]),
      ],
    })),
    results: [RESULT_ROWS_ENERGY, RESULT_ROWS_MONEY].map((keys, half) => ({
      headers: [
        t(half === 0 ? 'economics.section_energy' : 'economics.section_money'),
        t('economics.unit'),
        e.istName,
        pointName(e.pump),
      ],
      rows: keys
        .map((k) => e.rows.find((r) => r[0] === k)!)
        .filter(Boolean)
        .map(([key, label, unit, ist, vals]) => ({
          cells: [label, e.unitLabel(unit), ist, vals[0]],
          color:
            SIGNED_ROWS.has(key) && vals[0] !== '–' ? (vals[0].startsWith('-') ? RED : GREEN) : '',
        })),
    })),
    sens_explain: e.sensExplain,
    size_explain: e.sizeExplain,
    summary: e.summaries[0],
    figures: [e.figures.bar, e.figures.price, e.figures.npv, e.figures.sens, e.figures.size],
    // Raw numbers for the comparison page.
    numbers: {
      capex: e.variants[0].capex,
      npv: e.results[0].npv,
      saving1: e.results[0].saving1,
      payback: e.results[0].payback,
      co2_saving: e.results[0].co2Saving,
    },
  };
}
